description: Fix retry bias in 7 metacognition notebooks (calibration, control, epistemic_humility, error_detection, fok, jol, learning_monitoring)
steps: Step 1: Read repo/docs/RETRY_BIAS_ISSUE.md for the fix pattern (strip think tags, parse locally, no retry LLM call)
Step 2: For each of the 7 affected metacog notebooks, open the corresponding task_*.py in repo/benchmarks/metacognition/

Step 3: Replace every schema= parameter usage and retry/except pattern with: single llm.prompt() call, _strip_think() helper to remove <think>...</think> tags, regex JSON extraction, local parsing — no second LLM call
Step 4: Update each corresponding .ipynb notebook to match the fixed .py file (sync notebook cells with .py source)
Step 5: Validate all 7 notebooks pass jupyter nbconvert --to notebook syntax check
Step 6: Run one quick smoke test (metacog_fok) against Bedrock Claude Sonnet to confirm the fix works end-to-end

description: Re-run all 9 metacognition benchmarks across 10 models with full Q&A transcript logging
steps: Step 1: Modify repo/scripts/run_benchmark_bedrock.py to save full prompt+response text per question per model (not just aggregate scores). Output to repo/sub-workflows/metacognition/results/qa_transcripts/<benchmark>/<model>.jsonl with fields: question_id, prompt, response, parsed_answer, correct_answer, score
Step 2: Clear all cached .run.json files for metacog benchmarks in repo/results/ and repo/benchmarks/metacognition/
Step 3: Run all 9 metacog benchmarks sequentially across 10 models using the modified runner. Use 300s timeout per benchmark, 900s for DeepSeek-R1. Run models sequentially to avoid OOM
Step 4: Verify 89/90 transcripts exist (Ministral 3B calibration expected to fail). Spot-check 3 random transcripts for completeness
Step 5: Generate repo/sub-workflows/metacognition/results/score_matrix_metacog_v2.csv from the new run

description: Per-benchmark analysis for external monitoring tier: canary, epistemic_humility, error_detection
steps: Step 1: Load Q&A transcripts from repo/sub-workflows/metacognition/results/qa_transcripts/ for canary, epistemic_humility, error_detection
Step 2: For each benchmark compute: mean, std, range, ceiling/floor effects from score_matrix_metacog_v2.csv

Step 3: Review 5 Q&A transcripts per benchmark (pick: highest-scoring model, lowest-scoring model, mid-range model, one where score seems surprising, one random). Document: correct scoring examples, incorrect scoring examples, parsing artifacts
Step 4: Assess ground truth validity — are correct answers actually correct? Flag any debatable items with item IDs
Step 5: Write recommendation for each: keep as-is, revise specific items (list IDs), adjust scoring formula, or drop. Include rationale
Step 6: Save analysis to repo/sub-workflows/metacognition/results/analysis_external_monitoring.md

description: Per-benchmark analysis for self-monitoring tier: epistemic_revision, learning_monitoring, control
steps: Step 1: Load Q&A transcripts from repo/sub-workflows/metacognition/results/qa_transcripts/ for epistemic_revision, learning_monitoring, control
Step 2: For each benchmark compute: mean, std, range, ceiling/floor effects from score_matrix_metacog_v2.csv
Step 3: Review 5 Q&A transcripts per benchmark (highest, lowest, mid-range, surprising, random). Document: correct scoring, incorrect scoring, parsing artifacts
Step 4: Assess ground truth validity — flag debatable items with IDs
Step 5: Write recommendation for each: keep as-is, revise items (list IDs), adjust scoring, or drop
Step 6: Save analysis to repo/sub-workflows/metacognition/results/analysis_self_monitoring.md

description: Per-benchmark analysis for prospective self-assessment tier: jol, fok, calibration
steps: Step 1: Load Q&A transcripts from repo/sub-workflows/metacognition/results/qa_transcripts/ for jol, fok, calibration
Step 2: For each benchmark compute: mean, std, range, ceiling/floor effects from score_matrix_metacog_v2.csv
Step 3: Review 5 Q&A transcripts per benchmark (highest, lowest, mid-range, surprising, random). Document: correct scoring, incorrect scoring, parsing artifacts, BSS computation validity
Step 4: Assess ground truth validity — for calibration, verify procedural question answers are correct. For FOK/JOL, verify gamma correlation computation handles edge cases (zero denominators)
Step 5: Write recommendation for each: keep as-is, revise items, adjust scoring, or drop. Special attention to calibration floor effect (6/10 models score 0.000)
Step 6: Save analysis to repo/sub-workflows/metacognition/results/analysis_prospective_assessment.md

description: Write metacognition track improvement plan based on per-benchmark analyses
steps: Step 1: Read the three analysis files: analysis_external_monitoring.md, analysis_self_monitoring.md, analysis_prospective_assessment.md from repo/sub-workflows/metacognition/results/

Step 2: Compile all revision/scoring/drop recommendations across 9 benchmarks into a priority-ordered list. Rank by: (a) impact on overall track discrimination, (b) severity of scoring bugs, (c) ground truth issues
Step 3: For each recommended fix, estimate effort (small: <30min code change, medium: 30-60min redesign, large: >60min with re-run needed) and whether model re-runs are required

Step 4: Group fixes into implementation batches: Batch 1 = scoring/parsing fixes (no item changes, no re-run needed), Batch 2 = item revisions (re-run needed), Batch 3 = benchmark redesigns (re-run + revalidation needed)
Step 5: Save improvement plan to repo/sub-workflows/metacognition/IMPROVEMENT_PLAN.md with sections: Summary, Priority List, Batch 1/2/3 details, Remaining Known Limitations, Estimated Total Effort
